The judge should exclude the evidence of the man’s prior similar cases if it is offered only to show propensity or likelihood that he molested this child, because such character evidence is generally inadmissible. It may be admitted only if it is relevant to a proper purpose such as motive, intent, plan, identity, or absence of mistake, and if its probative value is not substantially outweighed by unfair prejudice.  
CONFIDENCE: 95
